newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Rebels push further into Zaire's copper province.
newsitem.headline: Rebels push further into Zaire's copper province.

text.p: Zaire has rushed troops to defend another town in the copper province of Shaba from Tutsi-led rebels heading there, a defense ministry official said Tuesday.
Rebels were trying to reach Moba, about 90 miles from the more important Lake Tanganyika port of Kalemie, taken earlier by the guerrillas, the official said in Kinshasa.

"The rebels are trying to get to Moba. They have taken another route to the interior of Kalemie to get there but we have naval units there who will resist," said the official who asked not to be identified.
"We are sending in reinforcements by train from the military bases in Kamina and Lubumbashi," he added.

Zaire earlier acknowledged more battlefield losses to Tutsi-led rebels who launched an armed campaign from Zaire's eastern borderlands in October. They now hold a 600-mile strip stretching into the copper province.
But deputy foreign minister Henri-Thomas Lokondo Yoka ruled out talks with rebels despite Zaire's concern about the latest setbacks including the fall of Kalemie on Lake Tanganyika.
Despite the loss of Kamelie, a key supply link for copper and cobalt mines around Lubumbashi 500 miles away, the government rejected the latest rebel calls for negotiations.

"They may be winning battles but they have not won the war," Lokondo Yoka tolf Reuters. "Of course we are concerned but we are in the process of taking measures to retake all the occupied areas. You will see in the days to come."
The sources told Reuters in Kigali rebels of Laurent Kabila's Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire were pursuing retreating soldiers toward Moba.

The government ordered a massive mobilisation and turned to its African allies for help after rebels extended their campaign and territory they hold from the borders of Rwanda and Uganda to the mineral-rich Shaba Province.

Ethnic Tutsis launched the war in provinces close to Rwanda and Uganda last October. They now control a strip stretching 600 miles into Shaba and Kabila says he wants to end the rule of President Mobutu Sese Seseko, in power since 1965.
A senior Defense Ministry official said Monday Togo, Chad and Morocco had accepted Mobutu's request for troops while Egypt agreed to send war materials.
Togo denied planning to send troops. Egypt said it had no defense ties with Zaire. There was no word from Chad or Morocco, where Zaire's veteran ruler Mobutu Sese Seko is visiting.

Zaire accuses neighboring Rwanda, Uganda and Burundi of sending their regular armies to back the rebels. Ethnic Tutsis originally took up arms after Zairian authorities threatened to uproot them to their ancestral homeland in Rwanda. Kabila now says he wants to end Mobutu's 31-year rule.
"We cannot negotiate with the rebels. They are, as you know, supported by certain countries," Lokonda Yoka said.
The army said Tuesday that Rwandan-backed rebels had defeated Zaire soldiers at Kalemie.
Residents in the capital Kinshasa in contact with the port before it fell told Reuters hundreds of members of the local population fled the town by train three days earlier.
They said residents had begun fleeing the town of Kongolo, 150 miles west of Kalemie in the same Shaba province, and also linked by rail to the provincial capital Lubumbashi.
Kalemie is a strategic commercial transit point with rail, air and lake connections to the entire region.
